Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Physical and mental actions are executed by the operational forces of material nature. However, an individual bewildered by ego misattributes these natural processes to themselves, foolishly assuming, 'I am the sole doer'.
Situation/Problem_Faced: The illusion of complete personal agency and control, leading to false pride, excessive personal burden, and anxiety.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna exposes the illusion of the false ego (ahankara). While material nature operates the physical and mental apparatus, the bewildered soul falsely claims full ownership of actions.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna receives a fundamental lesson on distinguishing true identity from environmental and physiological processes.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.De-centering Ego: Recognizing that personal identity is distinct from bodily and environmental conditioning
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Locus of Control: Balancing personal effort with an understanding of external natural factors
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Over-identification with Outcomes: Avoiding stress by realizing you are not the sole cause of every result

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Ahankara-vimudhatma (The soul bewildered by false ego)
Karta aham iti manyate (Falsely thinking 'I am the doer')

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: All physical activities are performed by the modes of material nature. The soul, blinded by false ego, mistakenly believes itself to be the independent creator and controller of action.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Believing you are in total control of every outcome creates immense stress and inflated ego. Recognizing that your body, brain, and environment are part of a broader system allows you to act responsibly without taking excessive personal blame or credit.
